steps.name: Lab Director
steps.text: ...I'm afraid I have to stop you.

steps.name: Lab Director
steps.text: The Marshal has ordered strict secrecy over New Lab Six's research. Even an inspection of research progress—

steps.name: Arrogant Officer
steps.text: You are Alita Valueva? Director of this lab?

steps.name: Alita
steps.text: ...Yes, sir.

steps.name: Arrogant Officer
steps.text: Then you know that the Marshal has given her son, Anatoliy Svetlanov, full authority over the Kushkina Project.

steps.name: Arrogant Officer
steps.text: And you must know that the Generalik has reached the end of his patience with your lack of progress.

steps.name: Alita
steps.text: I have already explained to the Marshal that energy supplies have been highly inconsistent since the beginning of the Originium vein crisis.

steps.name: Alita
steps.text: As the research progresses, its demand for energy grows... just as one cannot make butter from water, experiments cannot continue without the right conditions.

steps.name: Arrogant Officer
steps.text: On the unauthorized transfer of energy—

steps.name: Alita
steps.text: That is exactly what I'm trying to say—

steps.name: Alita
steps.text: I've submitted a report on the matter to the Marshal, and personally overseen the shutdown of potential channels. It will not happen again.

steps.name: Alita
steps.text: Please explain it to the Generalik. I would be happy to submit a copy of the report for the Marshal to him.

steps.name: Arrogant Officer
steps.text: Ah... I'm sure he would be very interested.

steps.name: Arrogant Officer
steps.text: The Generalik's temperament is unlike the Marshal's. He wants to see New Lab Six's effectiveness and loyalty.

steps.name: Arrogant Officer
steps.text: See those in your husband's lab, for example... the smallest of leaks has already ensured that they will never have the trust of the First Army again.

steps.name: Arrogant Officer
steps.text: Do not repeat their mistakes.

steps.name: Arrogant Officer
steps.text: Give her the letter.

steps.name: Accompanying Soldier
steps.text: Yes, sir.

steps.name: Alita
steps.text: Sir, this is...

steps.name: Arrogant Officer
steps.text: Data provided by a friend of the Marshal's. The Generalik has instructed me to give it to you, so that the lab can improve upon Kushkina according to the concepts contained within.

steps.name: Arrogant Officer
steps.text: Also, the test animal on the loose is causing panic amongst some of the civilians. The Generalik would like you to resolve this matter immediately, or at the very least find out the cause... do you understand?
Alita takes a deep breath. Her fingers touch the letter sealed with Grypherburg's standard Hippogryph seal, and nods without hesitation, suppressing her doubts.

steps.name: Alita
steps.text: I understand... please tell the Generalik that I will do my duty and complete the goals as quickly as possible.

steps.name: Alita
steps.text: Phew—

steps.name: Alita
steps.text: They're gone. You can come out now.

steps.name: Ursus Researcher
steps.text: Thank you, professor. They would have been suspicious if they saw me.

steps.name: Alita
steps.text: I'm the one who should thank you, Marat.

steps.name: Alita
steps.text: You're taking a huge risk, helping me look for data while acting as the Army's science consultant. I don't know how to thank you.

steps.name: Ursus Researcher
steps.text: I'm not just doing it for you. I'm curious why they're suddenly recruiting so many Infected all of a sudden, myself.

steps.name: Alita
steps.text: Did you find anything?

steps.name: Ursus Researcher
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Ursus Researcher
steps.text: They're using those Infected to provide 'energy' for the project.

steps.name: Alita
steps.text: Are you saying—

steps.name: Ursus Researcher
steps.text: In the literal sense of the word.

steps.name: Duty Soldier
steps.text: Passphrase.

steps.name: Delivering Soldier
steps.text: 'Snow made from iron does not burn.'

steps.name: Duty Soldier
steps.text: You're three minutes late. Be careful next time. The ones inside are not as well-tempered as we are.

steps.name: Delivering Soldier
steps.text: Not much we can do about it. There are fewer and fewer usables, and harder to acquire the goods. The higher-ups would rather those who are in less serious condition keep working.

steps.name: Duty Soldier
steps.text: They'll come down on us if quota's not met.

steps.name: Delivering Soldier
steps.text: We should worry about ourselves. We'll end up like those in the truck if we get infected ourselves.

steps.name: Duty Soldier
steps.text: What's that sound—

steps.name: Delivering Soldier
steps.text: Huh? I didn't hear anything.

steps.name: Delivering Soldier
steps.text: Well, it's about time this old bucket got an overhaul.

steps.name: Duty Soldier
steps.text: Keep moving, don't waste time.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Phew... that was close!

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: I can't get any closer with all that jamming... not after I almost lost No.128.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Let me see... no, there's too much noise.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: The drones start acting up within about 1km of this area. They can still fly, but real-time video is inoperable, and other preloaded functions are also disabled.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: There's something really weird about this wall!
Before the Rhodes Island team lies a tall, grey wall that stretches as far as the eye could see. The marks that rain has left upon it glow metallic blue under the grey skies.
Closure looks up at the wall that blocks out half the sky. Its size and weight is oppressive, even at a distance.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Good thing the patrols don't come around here, and we haven't seen any other locals approach. Do they all pretend the wall doesn't exist?

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: It stretches out from downtown. Who could fail to see it?

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: Military-grade ECM equipment is deployed throughout the wall. It far exceeds what a normal military facility requires to prevent accidental trespassing.

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: It's strange.

options: If the First Army is determined to stop cooperating with the legislature...

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: We'll be spending our entire stay dealing with this equipment, if we don't think of something.

steps.name: Raidian
steps.text: I have some discoveries, or should I say, hypotheses.

steps.name: Raidian
steps.text: I tried to use my Arts this morning, focusing on specific human signal bands to reduce workload.

steps.name: Raidian
steps.text: I thought about giving up after several attempts came up empty before I discovered a band that periodically disappears before reappearing.

steps.name: Raidian
steps.text: It occurs at regular intervals, with two iterations up to this point.

steps.name: Raidian
steps.text: Did you see anything go through the wall?

options: But we didn't see what the payload was.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: I remember it. The searchlight followed it without setting off any alarms. I thought I was lucky, but it seems strange now that I think of it.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: If the curfew was imposed in order to covertly transport something behind the wall—

options: It may be the only way for us to sneak in.

steps.name: Raidian
steps.text: If we want to use it to sneak in, we could lay in wait along its path.

steps.name: Raidian
steps.text: Come back, Doctor. We need to plan our next steps.

steps.name: Raidian
steps.text: This time, I need to be present.

steps.name: Tonya
steps.text: Doctor!

steps.name: Tonya
steps.text: You said you found an abnormal patient? Is he—
The doctor shakes her head before Tonya could finish.

steps.name: Nadezhda
steps.text: You came sooner than I thought, Tonya, but...

steps.name: Nadezhda
steps.text: See for yourself.
The doctor lifts the quarantine tarp and reveals a body covered by white cloth.
Lifeless like a marble statue.
Then, she lifts the cloth and folds it up...
Tonya's nails dig into her palm. She has seen death plenty of times, but never one as terrible as this...
She sees the familiar face, the soul long gone from it, but not the slightest sign of pain or struggle upon it.
The brow is relaxed, the eyelids closed, the slightly curved lips highlighting the lines of age, freezing everything into what appears to be a benevolent smile.
Then, the neck, the shoulders, the torso... Tonya's eyes go wide.
Bright crystals extrude from the pale skin, reflecting a yellowish glow in the ceiling lamp's light.

steps.name: Tonya
steps.text: No, no, doctor...

steps.name: Tonya
steps.text: It's not the same as what happened to my sister...
A quiet sigh answers her in the empty operating room.

steps.name: Nadezhda
steps.text: The symptoms are indicative of an acute Oripathy onset.

steps.name: Nadezhda
steps.text: But he had demonstrated similar symptoms as your sister when he first came. If your sister was in the initial stages, he was in the final stages.

steps.name: Tonya
steps.text: Could the illness be... with Oripathy...

steps.name: Tonya
steps.text: But people with Oripathy don't die so peacefully!

steps.name: Nadezhda
steps.text: You're right. Oripathy patients often experience unimaginable pain when they die, as their bodies disintegrate.

steps.name: Nadezhda
steps.text: I performed a comprehensive check before you came...

steps.name: Nadezhda
steps.text: His vocal cords were not swollen, nor were there any scratch marks on his body. His muscles were relaxed, with no sign of painful spasms prior to death, nor any sign of disintegration...

steps.name: Nadezhda
steps.text: But all these questions do not change the fact that he died from Oripathy.

steps.name: Nadezhda
steps.text: This points to the possibility that his condition, and whatever is affecting your sister, is simply a variant of Oripathy.
Tonya was no longer listening. Her ears are ringing, and her eyes refuse to avert their gaze from the smile on the dead's face.
It is neither release from suffering, nor hope for the end, only a numb comfort.
His consciousness, his soul, all his emotions towards the land, even fear itself, have been soothed over by a gentle yet irresistible force.
And the only clue, the last hope to discover the truth about the strange illness, is gone with the patient's passing.

steps.name: Tonya
steps.text: ...What's that sound, doctor?

steps.name: Nadezhda
steps.text: What sound? I don't hear anything.

steps.name: Tonya
steps.text: I think I hear my sister crying... is she calling to me?

steps.name: Nadezhda
steps.text: Look at me, Tonya. Your sister is in isolation. I keep my eye on her every day and hum lullabies to put her to bed. She'll be fine.

steps.name: Nadezhda
steps.text: She's still sleeping. Children her age need sleep to recover. Whatever you're hearing, it's not her... take a deep breath.

steps.name: Tonya
steps.text: No, doctor, it's not that...

steps.name: Tonya
steps.text: It was raining heavily that night. I ran through three streets to bring her to you. She was so light, like an empty basket...

steps.name: Tonya
steps.text: But her head, pressed against my forehead, was burning, so hot it made my tremble...

steps.name: Tonya
steps.text: I still don't know what she's sick with. It wouldn't even leave me with a speck of hope!

steps.name: Tonya
steps.text: Why did it do this to her, to us...

steps.name: Tonya
steps.text: What did we do wrong?

steps.name: Nadezhda
steps.text: Tonya!

steps.name: Borislav
steps.text: Go—

steps.name: Borislav
steps.text: Doctor, we have to go! The soldiers have found this place! They're already downstairs. We'll need to take the emergency passage.

steps.name: Nadezhda
steps.text: What about Nina?

steps.name: Borislav
steps.text: In the incubator. Should we grab her?

steps.name: Borislav
steps.text: ...What's going on with Tonya?

steps.name: Nadezhda
steps.text: Give me a hand and get her up. Nina cannot leave the incubator at this time. We can only pray they'll show mercy to a child.

steps.name: Nadezhda
steps.text: Leave the rest. We can come back for it.

steps.name: Borislav
steps.text: So light...

steps.name: Borislav
steps.text: What about this one?

steps.name: Nadezhda
steps.text: We have to leave him.

steps.name: Nadezhda
steps.text: He might even buy us some time.

steps.name: Nadezhda
steps.text: Let's go.

steps.name: Nadezhda
steps.text: I left a sign for the others in the operating room.

steps.name: Impatient Soldier
steps.text: Gah... they got away again.

steps.name: Cautious Soldier
steps.text: Doesn't matter. Our primary mission is not to arrest people. They always get wind of things, like those 'musbeasts' in the underground layers.

steps.name: Cautious Soldier
steps.text: Found anything other than the kid?

steps.name: Impatient Soldier
steps.text: No.

steps.name: Cautious Soldier
steps.text: Did you search every room thoroughly?

steps.name: Impatient Soldier
steps.text: I—

steps.name: Excited Voice
steps.text: —Found it!

steps.name: Excited Voice
steps.text: There's a body in the operating room, but...

steps.name: Cautious Soldier
steps.text: Take it anyway.

steps.name: Cautious Soldier
steps.text: Be careful not to knock off any pieces.

steps.name: Impatient Soldier
steps.text: I'm taking these meds too.

steps.name: Cautious Soldier
steps.text: There's no date on them, who knows if they work at all. But suit yourself.

steps.name: Impatient Soldier
steps.text: Better than nothing.

steps.name: Impatient Soldier
steps.text: Doing this stuff every day... I don't want to wait for that factory scrip khuinya to get my sleeping pills.

spans.text: Doing this stuff every day... I don't want to wait for that factory scrip

steps.text: That one again?
Yeah.
Something happened during fresh-air time? Refused to kneel, or—
Offered to take punishment for the others when boss was punishing the Infected.
Again... carry the suka up.

steps.name: Grumbling Soldier
steps.text: Hey, still breathing?

steps.name: Grumbling Soldier
steps.text: Zhopa, they're gonna kill someone if they go on like this.

spans.text: , they're gonna kill someone if they go on like this.

steps.name: Taciturn Soldier
steps.text: The Generalik wants the Infected alive...

steps.name: Grumbling Soldier
steps.text: Tell the tupoi Luzhin to explain to the Generalik. I'm sure he could spin a bunch of flowery words, considering it was the Generalik who stuck him in our squad to begin with.

spans.text: Luzhin to explain to the Generalik. I'm sure he could spin a bunch of flowery words, considering it was the Generalik who stuck him in our squad to begin with.

steps.name: Taciturn Soldier
steps.text: Watch your words. Luzhin is our superior officer, for now at least. The First Army's—

steps.name: Grumbling Soldier
steps.text: Honor? Discipline? As if there's any of that left in the First Army. Blyat, screw that svolotsch Generalik...

spans.text: Honor? Discipline? As if there's any of that left in the First Army.

steps.name: Grumbling Soldier
steps.text: Bleh, keep an eye on 'em, and call a medic at any signs of trouble—those pizdets animal doctors do nothing well except clean up dead bodies...

spans.text: Bleh, keep an eye on 'em, and call a medic at any signs of trouble—those
animal doctors do nothing well except clean up dead bodies...

steps.name: Grumbling Soldier
steps.text: But I bet this suka will last the night.

steps.name: Taciturn Soldier
steps.text: Shouldn't have defied us, eh?

steps.name: Calm Youth
steps.text: I can take it... leave the others alone.

steps.name: Taciturn Soldier
steps.text: Hey, you asked for it. Don't say we didn't warn you.

steps.name: Calm Youth
steps.text: I saw bandages on your arm while you were carrying me, and that wound on your head...

steps.name: Calm Youth
steps.text: Did you defy your own superior, Ratkov?

steps.name: Taciturn Soldier
steps.text: Don't push your luck. I'm only here because I was ordered to keep an eye on you. Don't presume to question the Generalik just because we've talked a couple of times.

steps.name: Calm Youth
steps.text: Sorry...

steps.name: Calm Youth
steps.text: I just happened to see similar marks on you, which made me think... perhaps we're not so different after all.
The youth fights the pain to take out a packet with blood-stained fingertips, dangling it in front of the soldier with a trembling hand.

steps.name: Taciturn Soldier
steps.text: What are you doing?

steps.name: Calm Youth
steps.text: For you. Medicine powder made from a plant that grows only on the Northern Tundra. Works wonders on wounds...

steps.name: Taciturn Soldier
steps.text: How did we not find it when we searched you?

steps.name: Calm Youth
steps.text: Survival wisdom that Ursus taught us... take it. I have enough for myself.

steps.name: Taciturn Soldier
steps.text: I know this medicine.

steps.name: Calm Youth
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Taciturn Soldier
steps.text: I grew up in Zavorsk. One time I got a gaping gash on my leg that almost reached the bone. My grandfather poured this medicine over the wound, and it only took one night for the wound to close.

steps.name: Taciturn Soldier
steps.text: My family gave me a bunch when I enlisted. It came in handy in the two years that I spent on the border fighting bandits, before I was transferred to the First Army.

steps.name: Taciturn Soldier
steps.text: I didn't expect to see it here.

steps.name: Calm Youth
steps.text: Zavorsk... it's near the Far North...

steps.name: Taciturn Soldier
steps.text: Yes. I haven't heard from my family ever since the Fourth Army's insurrection.

steps.name: Calm Youth
steps.text: Most of my companions came from the Northern Tundra.

steps.name: Calm Youth
steps.text: If I can meet up with them, I could ask them about your family—

steps.name: Taciturn Soldier
steps.text: There's no need.

steps.name: Taciturn Soldier
steps.text: I'm already breaking rules by talking to you like this.

steps.name: Taciturn Soldier
steps.text: I have to go. I can put in a request if there's anything you need.

steps.name: Calm Youth
steps.text: You said your grandfather used that medicine on you.

steps.name: Calm Youth
steps.text: The one who gave me the medicine said that only lumberjacks and hunters who live in the Northern Tundra forests know how to make it.

steps.name: Calm Youth
steps.text: Your grandfather—

steps.name: Taciturn Soldier
steps.text: He was a lumberjack. So was my father.

steps.name: Calm Youth
steps.text: While you joined the First Army. Good...

steps.name: Calm Youth
steps.text: I know many children of lumberjacks. At least you aren't learning how to bury other children of lumberjacks.
The soldier's shoulders twitch, as though he had been whipped.

steps.name: Calm Youth
steps.text: You know how many soldiers have claimed those forests for themselves, backed by the rich and powerful.

steps.name: Calm Youth
steps.text: They beat up and expelled those who lived in the forests, forcing them to leave the land which their ancestor had always lived, becoming homeless refugees, or willing slaves.

steps.name: Calm Youth
steps.text: No doubt your father and grandfather will be proud of you, seeing you grow up strong and healthy, escaping such cruel fate with your family...

steps.name: Taciturn Soldier
steps.text: What are you trying to say?

steps.name: Calm Youth
steps.text: My question for you is—whose son are you?

steps.name: Calm Youth
steps.text: Your grandfather, the lumberjack from Zavorsk...

steps.name: Calm Youth
steps.text: Did he heal your leg so that you can bend it to the oppressors, or stand with dignity like a true son of Ursus?

steps.name: Calm Youth
steps.text: I have no requests for you to pass on. I only ask that you remember that you are a child of Ursus, like me, like all of us.

steps.name: Calm Youth
steps.text: We will never bow to those who wield the whip. We fight for everyone who should not be whipped.

steps.name: Calm Youth
steps.text: If the day comes when you want to find out about your father and grandfather, I... *cough* *cough*—

steps.name: Taciturn Soldier
steps.text: Save your strength...

steps.name: Taciturn Soldier
steps.text: I'll pretend I didn't hear any of that. Whatever you wanted to say, save it.
Wake up, boss.

steps.name: Calm Youth
steps.text: Mm... what's going on...

steps.name: Miner
steps.text: Bozhe moi, your wounds... those monsters—!

steps.name: Calm Youth
steps.text: Doesn't matter... how did you get out? I thought we were all locked up.

steps.name: Miner
steps.text: All the doors got unlocked for some reason.

steps.name: Miner
steps.text: We came to find you as soon as we got out. No soldiers along the way. Maybe something's gone wrong. Anyway, it's our chance!

steps.name: Miner
steps.text: But can you move? Your injuries—

steps.name: Calm Youth
steps.text: Don't worry about me...

steps.name: Calm Youth
steps.text: We don't have a lot of time, no matter whatever's happened with the Army. We need to move immediately.

steps.name: Miner
steps.text: Here, hold onto me.

steps.name: Calm Youth
steps.text: Our people are all here... what's going on?

steps.name: Calm Youth
steps.text: It's you—

steps.name: Taciturn Soldier
steps.text: I talked to my mates. The guys on duty will leave a gap. You have ten minutes to get out.

steps.name: Calm Youth
steps.text: Thank you so much...

steps.name: Calm Youth
steps.text: Ratkov, If I hear anything about your family—

steps.name: Taciturn Soldier
steps.text: Forget it. We all know it's a long shot.

steps.name: Calm Youth
steps.text: What will you do? The general will undoubtedly punish you after we leave.

steps.name: Taciturn Soldier
steps.text: We will not submit so easily. Anatoliy no longer deserves our loyalty.

steps.name: Taciturn Soldier
steps.text: There is considerable discontent towards his behavior in the Army. He will pay for his outrages.

steps.name: Taciturn Soldier
steps.text: We've talked enough. Go, and don't waste this chance.

steps.name: Calm Youth
steps.text: ...Take care, Ratkov.

steps.name: Calm Youth
steps.text: I will remember you, son of a Zavorsk lumberjack.

steps.name: Tonya
steps.text: Hm...

steps.name: Nadezhda
steps.text: You're awake?

steps.name: Tonya
steps.text: Where are we? Nina—

steps.name: Nadezhda
steps.text: The soldiers came to the clinic. We only had time to get you out.

steps.name: Nadezhda
steps.text: We couldn't take your sister because she couldn't leave the incubator in her current state. I'm sorry.

steps.name: Tonya
steps.text: Ugh—

steps.name: Nadezhda
steps.text: Headache? It's normal after blacking out like that.

steps.name: Tonya
steps.text: Is Nina still there? Did they take her? I have to—

steps.name: Nadezhda
steps.text: I went back to the clinic when you were out cold.

steps.name: Tonya
steps.text: ...Doctor?

steps.name: Nadezhda
steps.text: Nina wasn't there. They took her. The good news is that they took the incubator too. The bad news is... we don't know where they took her.

steps.name: Nadezhda
steps.text: I understand you want to find her, and I'll do what I can to help, but—

steps.name: Nadezhda
steps.text: Promise me this, Tonya. You have to stay strong, even if you don't find her... the rest of your family need you. They look up to you.

steps.name: Crownslayer
steps.text: You want to know what you can do? There's always one thing, and only one thing—

steps.name: Crownslayer
steps.text: Find more evidence.

steps.name: Tonya
steps.text: Doctor, you're sure that Kirill had the same symptoms as Nina when he first came into your care, only more serious?

steps.name: Nadezhda
steps.text: If you believe me. There was a Cautus who could use healing Arts, who might have eased his pain at my request. No one else came into contact.

steps.name: Nadezhda
steps.text: The Oripathy progressed rapidly. And what happened to him doesn't look like the result of pain relief.

steps.name: Tonya
steps.text: Then I must find more evidence... and Nina.

steps.name: Tonya
steps.text: I must find Nina...

steps.name: Nadezhda
steps.text: What are you going to do?

steps.name: Tonya
steps.text: What I had to do.

steps.name: Raidian
steps.text: Target lost.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Target has left the surveillance area. Drone acquisition lost.

steps.name: Raidian
steps.text: That means it's now within one klick of the wall, near your position.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: The patrols have left. There should be a gap of about ten minutes along the road.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: I'm coming over, Amiya.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Got it!

steps.name: Raidian
steps.text: Watch out for the searchlights.

steps.name: Raidian
steps.text: Do you see a grey vehicle?

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: Not yet!

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Wait, I think—

options: Approaching from behind on the right side.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: I'm not there yet! Wait for me—

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: We haven't made a move yet. Stay safe, Closure.

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: I see it. Looks like a modified Infected tractor for use in the wilderness.

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: I've heard of military tractors ending up with the Infected after retirement. Not sure I've ever seen it go the other way.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: We'll have to get closer to find out.

steps.name: Raidian
steps.text: You'll fall out of comms if you get any closer.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Let's go in and figure it out from there.

steps.name: Raidian
steps.text: Very well. I'll reestablish communications once you're inside.

steps.name: Raidian
steps.text: Raidian out.

steps.name: Driver
steps.text: Guh...

steps.name: Driver
steps.text: The radio always goes out around these parts. Nothing to do when waiting for the door to open.

steps.name: Driver
steps.text: Didn't they say they were building a new base station? How's the signal still so lousy—

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: ...From this vantage point, we can't even see how the door opens, or what sort of security measures are present.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: We may have to get on the tractor before it gets swarmed by patrols and go inside with it.

options: I'm not sure I could make the jump...

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: No worries, I got you!

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: I think I'll need help too.

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: I can take Closure too.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Counting on you, Mon3tr.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: (Hushed) Quiet now and stay focused. Wait for my signal.

steps.name: Driver
steps.text: Why's it taking so long for the door to open today, bratan?

spans.text: Why's it taking so long for the door to open today,

steps.name: Tired Soldier
steps.text: Who are you calling bratan? I'm your baba.

steps.name: Tired Soldier
steps.text: You'll wait if you want to go in. They're still checking your creds.

steps.name: Driver
steps.text: Wasn't you here last night, baba.

steps.name: Tired Soldier
steps.text: Yeah, they reassigned everybody to the suburban factories. We're on three shifts a day now, don't even get to sleep.

steps.name: Tired Soldier
steps.text: Alright, you can go in—

steps.name: Tired Soldier
steps.text: *cough*—*cough*!

steps.name: Tired Soldier
steps.text: What's that—

steps.name: Driver
steps.text: ...Woah, we got a lunatic trying to attack the wall!

steps.name: Tired Soldier
steps.text: Attack on the wall! Need backup at Zone A! Repeat, need backup at Zone A!

steps.name: Tired Soldier
steps.text: There was an explosion, someone's trying to force their way through—

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: There's someone else here? Did we luck into unexpected help?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: No time to think about it now!

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Raidian has rendezvoused with us. Let's use the chaos to get on the tractor—

steps.name: Stern Soldier
steps.text: —Close the door! No one gets in!

steps.name: Stern Soldier
steps.text: Attention—

steps.name: Stern Soldier
steps.text: Crossbows ready!

steps.name: Driver
steps.text: W-Wait! Don't point those weapons at me! I'm just delivering stuff!

steps.name: Driver
steps.text: Ugh, I'm gonna miss my next stop—

steps.name: Stern Soldier
steps.text: Hold it!

steps.name: Driver
steps.text: I'm sorry, I-I really can't afford to be late!

steps.name: Raidian
steps.text: Looks like a twenty-four-man squad with potential reinforcements coming up. We need to get moving.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: (Whispers) Come, Doctor!

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: Doctor! Give me your hand!

steps.name: Stern Soldier
steps.text: —That one's trying to get inside! Fire!
For an instant, your cries seem to be drowned in the noise.
Before your hands grasp anything in the darkness, you see a somewhat familiar figure in protective gear run towards you.

steps.name: Tonya
steps.text: Stand firm.
The figure charges at you and lifts you up, until you manage to find Mon3tr's hand and get on the edge of the tractor.
Then it disappears before you have time to react.
You turn around to see the figure in protective gear clumsily trying to climb the tractor, only to fall back onto the ground—
Easy prey for the soldiers rushing in from a distance, crossbows raised.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Look out—

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Closure—
